### Diagnosis

The current bug report describes an issue where comparing a value to null using the unequal operator (!=) yields false inconsistently. The provided code snippet of the failing test method `testMapValueEquality()` in `JXPath151Test` shows that it calls the method `assertXPathValue(context, "map/b != map/a", Boolean.TRUE)`.

By looking at the code snippet of the method `newContext(Object contextBean)` in `JXPathContext`, it seems that the `JXPathContext` is created with a null XPath context and only the Java bean context is provided.

The issue in the failing test `testMapValueEquality()` could be related to how the `JXPathContext` is initialized with map values. When the JXPath context is created with a map that contains null values, the evaluation of expressions like `"map/b != map/a"` may behave unexpectedly due to the way null values are handled in the context of JXPath.

To resolve this issue, the handling of null values in `JXPathContext` or the expression evaluation mechanism in JXPath needs to be reviewed to ensure consistent behavior when comparing values to null.

### Possible Fix
- `org.apache.commons.jxpath.JXPathContext.newContext(java.lang.Object)`
